The band is tagged and the core-vs-premium split exists in boundaries, so this is not fabrication or a missing tag on the number itself; it is an untagged/undecomposable BASIS plus an over-generalized scope on the headline. The A2-answerer's reconstruction (~$4-8/kg back-solve, LOW confidence) is a legitimate arithmetic check, not new sourced content. The fix is mechanical: state the identity and scope the band A1/A2-core with A3 as a separate order-of-magnitude row.

judgments.topic: 25% USTER (evenness) vs ICI >=3-4 (pilling): are they a contradiction, and is the accept/reject precedence written

judgments.topic: spec names TWO 'dominant constraints' (dye-lot MOQ sizes the brand; post-wash pilling gate dominates) with no explicit tie-break when they collide

Two constraints each labeled 'dominant' with no written precedence, though capability 6 implies the resolution.
judgments.judge_reasoning: Confirmed. The collision IS resolvable via 'refuses a lot failing any hard gate' — the pilling gate is a HARD accept/reject VETO while the dye-lot MOQ is a SIZING cap, so they act on different axes and rarely truly conflict — but the spec presents them as co-equal 'dominators' without writing the veto-first-then-size ordering. decision_procedure step 7's singular 'the dominant constraint' is under-specified against two labeled dominators. One clarifying sentence, mechanical, no new numbers.
judgments.minimal_fix: Add to decision_procedure step 7 / conflicts_and_dominance: 'these act on different axes: the post-wash pilling gate is a HARD accept/reject VETO (a failing lot is rejected regardless of MOQ), while the dye-lot MOQ SIZES the colour count within the surviving passing options; on collision, the quality veto binds first, then the MOQ sizes.'
